answer: Spectral Cutoff uses edge-count saturation: each agent may maintain at most k verified links, and a new node's messages propagate only if its neighborhood's clustering stays above a threshold. Fake identities can't manufacture the dense, mutually-reinforcing neighborhoods real agents form, so sybils sit on the dune of low connectivity and their signals die out. The willow of trusted clusters bends around them, ignoring the whisper of isolated nodes. Attackers must pay to build genuine overlapping links per identity.
